value: \$ dxc -T ps_6_0 -E main -fcgl \S+\.hlsl[\s\S]*\.hlsl:\d+:\d+: error: (?!local resource not guaranteed)
note:
POLARITY IS INVERTED. A match here means the FRONT END diagnoses the code -- i.e. the thing the issue's title asks for has been implemented. `no-repro` is therefore the reproduction of #3726 and `repro` would be the fix. Read every history line for this predicate with that in mind.

How it works: cmd.txt's third and last invocation is `-fcgl`, which emits high-level LLVM IR and never runs the DXIL lowering passes, so an `error:` in that invocation's block can only have come from the front end. The regex anchors on that invocation's `$ dxc ...` header line, which triage.py writes before each command, and then looks for a source-located diagnostic anywhere after it -- the -fcgl invocation is last, so 'after it' is exactly 'from it'. Message text is NOT pinned, because the whole point is to detect a diagnostic that does not exist yet and whose wording cannot be guessed.

Why not simply test for a `file:line:col: error:` prefix anywhere: it does not distinguish the layers. The DXIL back-end error is printed WITH that prefix on main (`repro.hlsl:15:10:`) via dxilutil::EmitErrorOnInstruction, and WITHOUT it on v1.4.1907. The negative lookahead excludes that one message as belt-and-braces in case an old release's -fcgl reaches further than main's does.

The filename is not pinned in either half, so controls run with `--shader` still exercise it.

CONTROLS: control-sema-mismatch.hlsl is the positive control -- the identical assignment with mismatched resource types, which Sema does reject (`cannot convert from 'Texture2D<float4>' to '__restrict SamplerState'`) -- and it MUST match (variant-sema-mismatch-*--match-sema.txt, --expect match). Without it, a predicate that can never fire is indistinguishable from a compiler that never diagnoses. control-correct.hlsl must NOT match (--expect no-match), proving it does not fire on everything.

KNOWN CLASSIFICATION ARTEFACT: on v1.4.1907 this predicate's probe is demoted to `invalid-probe`, because that release answers `SPIR-V CodeGen not available` to cmd.txt's SECOND invocation and classify() applies the feature-absence marker to the whole capture. The -fcgl invocation on v1.4.1907 does run and exits 0 with no diagnostic, which is a valid datapoint; it is preserved separately as variant-fcgl-only-v1.4.1907.txt.
